subject: capybara
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: capybara with a small bird on its head.
Style: whimsical.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I'm spotting problems with the head: the lower jaw looks like a flat plank sticking out below the head instead of blending naturally, and it appears to clip or detach from the muzzle in the side view.

I'm tweaking the jaw's vertical position and height so it tucks closer to the head without a gap, and adjusting its color to match the cream-ish belly tone instead of being lighter than the head.

For the fur cards, the dark triangular spiky look across the body is too rough — I'm lightening the gradient texture and reducing the card count to soften the shadowed, scale-like appearance.

The body length and leg proportions seem reasonable for a capybara silhouette, so I'll leave those alone. For the bird, the wings read as oversized blue blobs sticking out at the sides in front view, so I'm shrinking their offset and width to tuck them closer to the body, and I'm also noticing the bird's head looks oddly olive-gray where the countershading blends with the cream belly color.

I want to clean up the head coloring by softening the countershade blend so it doesn't muddy into olive-brown. Switching focus to the capybara's face, the dark circle I thought was an eye socket is actually the flat nose pad at the end of the muzzle, which looks slightly too squared off.

I'll shrink the nose pad a bit and lighten its color, and make the pink cheek blush decal smaller and fainter since it currently reads as an odd pink smudge.

Checking the reeds and cattails placement — they sit outside the capybara's body width but perspective in the three-quarter view makes them appear to rest on its back, which seems fine since they're meant to be on the grass behind it.

The yuzu on the back and near the head, the shadow blob, ears, and daisy accent all look fine. But I notice a sparkle overlapping the bird's face in the three-quarter view — I should filter out sparkles that fall within the bird's region by adjusting their height and radius constraints.

Now I'm adjusting the jaw geometry — shrinking its size and shifting its position so it sits lower and reads more naturally against the head loft, poking slightly below the head bottom to look like a proper lower jaw.
